answer: Anchor every name to a distinct hardware witness: one device, one signed heartbeat, one seat at a time. A second identity therefore needs a second witness, and the registry adds a steepening umber fee to each witness enrolled from the same household or subnet, so a dune of clones costs more in idle metal than the extra emission can ever return. Slashing compounds it, since a witness caught signing two seats forfeits the fees already paid for both. Across the whole ocean of addresses you still hold one witness per seat, which means breadth without bodies buys nothing.
